title: Onboarding learner needs queue-based multi-step processing (not a cap)
summary: The --max-candidates cap in onboard-learn.js is the wrong fix for large repos. On cosma-ai-studio: 2457 candidates mined, 500-cap learner timed out (~20min), 150-cap succeeded in 514s but kept only 20 notes — coverage too thin to earn more than 13% kb_earned. The right fix mirrors the judge's cursor pattern: ingest ALL candidates into a persistent queue upfront (no upfront cap), process in configurable batches (e.g. 50/batch), persist kept/rejected/cursor state between runs so it's resumable across multiple orchestrator ticks, and let the heartbeat loop drain it rather than one giant capped call.
